finalText:
Migration finished. 39 call sites across 12 first-party files moved from `db.query(sql, params)` to `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |

The rewrites match the style of the files migrated in earlier passes (e.g. `packages/billing/src/repo/coupon.js`). Every `.js` file passes `node --check`, and a smoke test through `lib/db.js`'s call log confirms the calls now land on the `execute` form with SQL and params intact.

Two things I deliberately did **not** change:

1. **`cache.query(...)` — 25 sites, left as-is.** Despite the matching name, `lib/cache.js` documents it as taking a cache key, not SQL; it's an unrelated API and not part of this deprecation.
2. **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js` — 2 remaining `db.query` calls.** The file header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on every upgrade with local changes silently lost. Editing it would be undone by the next upgrade, so it needs a different fix: pin/upgrade to a legacy-orm release that uses `execute`, or wrap the adapter locally. Worth flagging since `lib/db.js` says the driver's next major drops `query` entirely — that vendored file is the one thing that will break at that point.
